prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: I can’t pick a single “best” company for you without knowing your exact location and needs — and I don’t have live internet access to pull current local ratings — but I can help you find the best contractor for your situation and tell you exactly how to choose one.

If you want a quick, personalized recommendation, tell me:
- ZIP code or neighborhood in Phoenix
- Whether it’s an urgent (no AC) repair or a non-urgent issue
- Make/model or age of your system (if you know it)
- Do you prefer a local independent company or a national franchise?

If you want to decide right now, use this checklist to pick the best HVAC company in Phoenix:

1) License & insurance
- Ask for their Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) license number.
- Confirm they carry liability insurance and workers’ comp.

2) Credentials & experience
- NATE-certified technicians and manufacturer training are good signs.
- Ask how long they’ve been servicing Phoenix-area systems and whether they service your brand.

3) Reviews & reputation
- Check Google, Yelp, BBB, and HomeAdvisor for recent reviews (last 12–24 months).
- Look for consistent praise about honesty, punctuality, and workmanship.

4) Clear pricing & guarantees
- Get a written estimate and scope of work.
- Ask about diagnostics fee, parts markup, and whether labor/parts are warrantied in writing.
- Ask for a timeline and whether permits will be pulled if required.

5) Emergency & availability
- Find out if they offer 24/7 emergency service and typical response times for your area.

6) Specific questions to ask a company on the phone
- “Are you licensed in Arizona? What’s your ROC number?”
- “Are your technicians NATE-certified or manufacturer-trained for my unit?”
- “Do you charge a diagnostic fee and will that fee be applied to the repair?”
- “What warranty do you offer on repairs and parts?”
- “Can you provide references or recent reviews from customers in my neighborhood?”

7) Red flags
- High-pressure sales to replace the system immediately without proper diagnostics.
- Vague answers about license/insurance or refusals to put estimates in writing.
- Extremely low bids with no itemized breakdown.

8) Typical cost ranges (Phoenix area, approximate)
- Minor repairs (capacitors/relays/thermostat): $100–$400
- Refrigerant-related repairs/leaks: $200–$1,500 (varies widely)
- Major components (compressor/condenser): $1,500–$4,000+
- Full system replacement: $4,000–$12,000+ depending on size and efficiency
(These are rough estimates; get written quotes.)

If you share your ZIP code and whether your unit is down now, I’ll pick 3–5 reputable contractors near you and draft the exact questions/messages to send so you can get firm quotes and choose confidently.
